purpose: One fixed-cost-point falsifiable comparison of complete Spectral and Answer flows: whether answer-guided bounded rank renewal yields independent quality worth its additional cost at the same smaller final weight count.
necessary_interpretation: Poor initial data-free compression and restricted temporary adaptation can cause both flows to fail. A negative result closes this r200/b16/one-LR recipe, not all low-rank frameworks or answer information.

The added anchor exposures, one gate backward and up to two complete-candidate forward evaluations are separately paid. This is a full-procedure quality-cost comparison, not equal compute or isolated proxy causality.
Fallbacks, actual bank coverage, differing masks and selected masks must be reported. Lower selected-anchor NLL follows from the selection rule and is not a scientific success.

The DEV set is already explored. A passing point estimate or interval spanning zero establishes neither stable gain nor equivalence. No automatic PAS/full retraining, extra rank/LR/bank search or old-worker revival follows.
Known low-rank replacement, residual expansion/truncation, replay and gradient selection components do not establish a novel framework by combination or naming.
reviewer_actions: Necessary static text/source review and standard-library parsing/SHA only. No CPU admission, model, tensor, QA, GPU, scoring or bootstrap was run by the reviewer.
